A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReGenesis. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including figures, tables, and equations. Relocated sections and renumbered tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning and evaluation results on five in-domain and six out-of-domain tasks, alongside component ablations, model comparisons, and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds three-shot comparison results, guideline-level measurements, and analyses of generated reasoning strategies.

M1.justification: The 25-guideline adaptation, reasoning-structure generation, reasoning-path generation, answer filtering, selective hints, and fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Appendix A.8.3 interprets existing filtering as implicit guideline selection; it does not introduce another algorithmic step.

E1.justification: Sections 4.1.1 and 4.3.1 retain the same five in-domain and six OOD tasks. The added diagnostics reuse existing datasets, including GSM8K, NumGLUE, and OpenBookQA.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds an explicitly evaluated CoT Prompting (3-shot) comparison variant for the unfine-tuned Mistral model. The existing ground-truth-only, LMSI, LMSI with ground-truth filtering, and STaR comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: Added settings include three-shot inference and individual-guideline prompting. Section 5.5 and Appendix A.8.2 introduce a diagnostic protocol sampling 500 NumGLUE paths per method, then using Mistral to label and cluster their strategies without supplying the original guidelines. Existing training budgets, models, and accuracy-evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands investigation of the diversity hypothesis: GSM8K success/failure case studies and guideline sensitivity, strategy clustering in training paths and OOD outputs, and dataset-specific guideline preferences. These appear in Section 5.5 and Appendix A.8. The existing hint-placement ablation merely moves from Section 5.3 to Appendix A.1.

E5.justification: The dataset-mixture study retains its three-random-seed reporting in Figure 3 and the appendix. The added diagnostics introduce no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values and plotted results are retained, but v2 substantially expands diagnostic findings. Additions include three-shot scores in Table 2, such as 68.3% on GSM8K; guideline accuracies ranging from 20.30% to 53.45% in Table 26; and guideline proportions in Table 27. Appendix A.8.2 lists 10 versus 5 NumGLUE strategy clusters and 7 versus 4 OpenBookQA clusters for ReGenesis versus STaR. These are newly reported results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The formal method notation and existing z-score normalization remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs; the added mathematical expressions occur within empirical reasoning examples.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same self-improvement and OOD-generalization claims, including the reported approximately 6.1% OOD improvement versus a 4.6% baseline decline. The new analyses support the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v1 primarily hypothesizes that diverse task-agnostic guidance explains generalization. v2 interprets its new clustering as evidence that these strategies survive in task-specific paths and are learned for OOD inference. Appendix A.8 also attributes dataset-dependent performance to strategy alignment and describes filtering as implicitly selecting suitable guidelines. This substantially develops the mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-availability statement and repository address. Existing generation prompts, temperatures, hardware specifications, training hyperparameters, and LoRA information remain unchanged after appendix renumbering.

R1.justification: The related-work section and bibliography retain the same works and positioning relative to STaR, LMSI, supervised reasoning methods, and diverse prompting approaches. The additional STaR analyses extend empirical support without changing novelty framing.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact. v2 relocates the hint-placement section to Appendix A.1, adds Section 5.5 and Appendix A.8, updates cross-references, and revises publication and author notes. Existing material is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a row, and Tables 26–27 are added. The hint-placement table moves into the appendix, the Llama comparison is renumbered, and existing figures and tables reflow under the conference header. All four figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The added three-shot comparison, guideline measurements, and code-access information modestly improve transparency and give readers concrete checks absent from v1. The gains are limited by overinterpretation: model-generated clusters lack independent validation, and Appendix A.8.1 presents an incorrect equivalence between a 10% speed increase and a 10% time reduction as sound reasoning. The additional descriptive evidence improves assessability, but does not establish the claimed causal mechanism.
